name: Hairline lowering surgery

lead: Hairline lowering, also called forehead reduction, moves the hairline forward so the forehead looks shorter and the face better proportioned. The new hairline is visible once healed.

A surgeon cuts along the hairline, frees the scalp from deeper tissue, advances it and closes the wound. Published reports describe it mainly in women with a naturally high hairline and in facial feminization surgery, including a review of 29 women over 20 years and a series of 91 patients using bone-tunnelled sutures.

paras: It is performed by a plastic surgeon as a procedure with a healing period. A hair transplant over the scar is sometimes added afterwards to disguise it. Forum users compare it with hair transplants and hairstyling, and men discuss scar visibility and future hair loss as the main concerns.

Reported risks include a visible or widened scar, numbness, and limits on how far the scalp can advance. Surgery on a hairline that is still receding may leave the scar exposed later. Published series are small, mostly retrospective and mostly in women, so outcomes in men are less documented.

angle.text: Hairline lowering moves the hairline forward to shorten a tall forehead and rebalance facial proportions. Published series are mostly in women with a congenitally high hairline. The new hairline is visible after healing, and scar placement is the main discussion point.

lead: Hairline lowering surgery, also called forehead reduction or scalp advancement, is a cosmetic procedure that shortens the vertical height of the forehead by moving the hairline forward. A surgeon incises along the hairline, frees the scalp from deeper tissue, advances it and closes the wound [1][2]. Surgeons have described it chiefly for women with a congenitally high hairline and as one component of facial feminization surgery [3][4][1].

Published reports on the operation are mainly case series and technique descriptions. A retrospective review of 29 women treated by one surgeon over 20 years measured photographs before and after surgery [1], and a series of 91 patients described bone-tunnelling suture fixation of the advanced scalp [5]. Other reports cover forehead reduction in women and hair-transplant alternatives for Asian women with high foreheads [6][7].

In looksmaxxing communities the procedure is discussed as a hardmaxxing option for people who attribute a long forehead to hairline position. Users on looksmax.org describe both favourable results and concerns about scarring, and some argue it suits women better than men [8][9].
infobox: Incision along the hairline with scalp advancement

paras: In hairline lowering, the incision is placed along the front hairline, and the scalp is undermined and moved forward so that the hair-bearing skin covers part of the forehead [1][2]. Surgical reviews describe the aim as reducing forehead height and, in some designs, hiding the resulting scar within or just in front of the hairline [10][2].

Techniques differ in where the incision sits and how it is shaped. A plastic surgery paper on forehead lifting notes that an incision just in front of the hairline shortens the forehead but, unlike deliberate hairline advancement, does not by itself lower the hairline in the way a dedicated procedure does, and that standard brow-lift techniques can raise the hairline [11]. Reports in women describe irregular, hair-bearing-line incisions designed to look natural [1][6].

Most published series involve women with a naturally high hairline who want a shorter forehead [1][6]. A technique description with outcome analysis in female patients reports measured changes in forehead height [6].

Hairline lowering is among the procedures used in facial feminization surgery, where a high or receded hairline and a prominent brow are treated together with frontal bone reshaping and brow lifting [3][4]. A review of 220 consecutive patients describes the broader set of operations in this field [3].

A retrospective review of 29 women operated on by one surgeon reported standardized photograph measurements of the hairline before and after surgery [1]. A series of 91 patients evaluated hairline lowering with bone-tunnelling suture fixation and reported on its effectiveness and safety [5]. A further paper analysed surgical details and outcomes in female patients undergoing aesthetic forehead reduction [6].

Hair transplantation has also been studied as an alternative way to lower the frontal hairline, including a series in Asian women with high foreheads [7], and reviews discuss transplantation techniques in transgender patients [12]. These reports are largely retrospective and uncontrolled, and none is a randomized trial.

The scar along the hairline is the most discussed drawback in the surgical and forum discussion. Reviews of the technique address scar placement and closure as central to the design [10][2]. A user on looksmax.org who describes extensive research argued that scars vary between individuals, can stretch, and may be visible in some lighting or after swimming, and that results shown online may be flattering because of makeup and photography [9]. Another user who had the operation reported a red line during healing that eventually became essentially unnoticeable [8].

Because the operation is mostly described in women, whose hairlines are generally stable, forum commentators argue that in men the possibility of later recession complicates planning; they suggest assessing whether the hairline is stable before any surgical or transplant approach [13][9].

Users on looksmax.org discuss the procedure in guides, personal result threads and cautionary threads. One long guide describes first deciding whether a perceived large forehead comes from the hairline or the face's proportions, then comparing hairstyling, hair transplants and surgery [13]. Result posts describe the operation as helpful but sometimes costly relative to the change achieved [8]. A critical thread argues that for most men it carries drawbacks that surgeons do not emphasise [9]. Other threads discuss cost and low-priced overseas offers, which are mentioned here only as a topic of discussion.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, hairline lowering is discussed as a hardmaxxing alternative to hair transplants for a long forehead, with debate centring on the scar and on whether it suits men [13][8][9].

claims.claim: A tall forehead is often a hairline issue that surgery can fix.
The scar makes it a poor choice for most men.
A hair transplant over the scar can disguise it.
The hairline must be stable before any surgical option.

timeline.event: A plastic surgery paper discusses hairline lowering during forehead rejuvenation, noting that standard techniques can raise the hairline [11].
A 20-year single-surgeon review of hairline lowering in 29 women is published [1].
A case report combines hairline lowering with frontal sinus reshaping and brow lift in a transgender woman [4].
A series of 91 patients evaluates bone-tunnelling suture fixation [5].
